title: Lateral refactor ideas + PR follow-ups (scratchpad)
content:
Quick context: this is a scratchpad for a set of related PRs that touched batching, KV cache eviction, and a small API change to the Realtime router. I wanted to capture follow-ups, things I noticed in review but didn't block on, and a couple of lateral refactor ideas that would make future reviews much easier (especially around tests and observable signals).

High-level summary of outstanding things (actionable):
- INF-723 follow-up (owner: Jordan) — add an e2e perf benchmark that exercises long-prefix KV cache hits. Right now CI only runs short-sequence throughput; we need a ~1k-step prefix test to catch regressions. priority: high.
- Add a small guard in router: reject incompatible model-variant fallbacks for cross-region routing (owner: Samir). This was the root cause of the silent degradation we saw in canary run yesterday. priority: medium.
- Post-merge cleanup for PR-1428 (owner: Maya) — remove dead flags and consolidate the quantization toggle list. Add a migration note to the deploy runbook. priority: low.

Review checklist (my personal quick heuristic to scan a runtime/serving PR):
- Correctness: unit tests for the new logic? If not, is there a compelling reason (networking/e2e complexity)?
- Behavioral invariants: do new code paths preserve cache invariants (kv size accounting, hit counters)? If a new eviction condition is added, is it deterministic?
- Observability: new counters/metrics/traces for control flow branches. If a new fallback is introduced, ensure there's a trace tag that surfaces when it happens.
- Backwards compatibility: API surface (router options, model variant names) — add compatibility tests or deprecation note.
- Performance: microbenchmark or a reasoned cost model for increased allocations/locks. CPU-bound loops should have flamegraph evidence if they changed.
- Config safety: feature-flag defaults should be conservative; ensure rollout + kill-switch in config.
- Tests: unit coverage + small integration smoke e2e in CI pipeline with a mocked backend.

Common smells I kept seeing in these PRs:
- Large functions that mix request validation, routing logic, and metrics emission. Suggest: split into router.validate(), router.route(), router.observe() with small pure helpers that are easily unit tested.
- Ad-hoc map-based caches without a single cache abstraction. We have 3 different LRU-like maps in serving-runtime; consolidate into Cache abstraction (interface + 2 implementations) so tests can inject deterministic behavior.
- Metrics litter: repeated conditionals that increment metrics inline. Move to a small observability utility to reduce noise and make consistent tag naming.

Lateral refactor proposals (short, cheap wins):
1) Small cache abstraction: 2–3 files, same public surface. Benefits: unified eviction semantics, single spot for instrumentation, easier to fake in CI. Risk: refactor touches hot path — keep performance identical by benchmarking before/after.
2) Router control flow states enum: replace a few stringly-typed states with an enum type (RouteDecision). Less error-prone and easier to trace. Cheap to implement.
3) Test harness for long-prefix KV behavior: standalone harness that can run locally and in CI with a small model stub that returns consistent KV keys. Would catch regressions like the one in INF-723.

Detailed notes from reading code (line-by-line highlights):
- file: router/realtime.go: around handleFallbacks() — fallback logic doesn't check model-compatibility flag. Potential for silent fallbacks when regional pool lacks quantized variants. Patch: add isCompatibleVariant(originVariant, fallbackVariant) check and early trace log. Notably, there is an existing compatibility matrix in modelmeta; reuse that function instead of duplicating logic.
- file: serving/cache/kv_map.go: size accounting increments happen after insertion; race if eviction triggered concurrently. Marked TODO: add atomic size counter or use mutex consistently. I left inline comment but didn't push block.
- file: serving/batching/batcher.go: continuousBatcher has an inner loop with sleep-based backoff; this can cause tail latency jitter. Consider switching to a condition variable or channel-based wake for new work.

Tests I would add before next release:
- deterministic eviction order test when multiple keys have same weight; simulate concurrent inserts.
- router fallback trace test: when fallback is chosen, assert trace contains fallback.reason and fallback.variant.
- batching high-load test: confirm batching latency p95 remains within threshold under synthetic load.

Follow-up PR sketch (low-effort):
- PR title: "router: add variant compatibility guard + trace tag for fallbacks"
- Files: router/realtime.go, router/realtime_test.go, trace/tags.go
- Changes: call modelmeta.IsVariantCompatible() before selecting fallback; when incompatible, continue to next candidate and emit trace tag fallback.variant_incompatible=true. Add unit tests for 3 scenarios. Estimated size: 40–80 LOC.

Notes for code-review comments I left (and why I didn't block):
- "consider extracting X": purely cosmetic but helpful long-term; left as a suggestion because current change is small and we need to get canary out.
- "missing metric for branch Y": flagged as a P1 for observability but not blocking because fallback still logged to admin logs.
- "potential race in cache size": left as inline FIXME with link to INF-723; it's nontrivial to fix immediately so I requested a follow-up ticket.

Misc ideas for future infra improvements (non-blocking, long-term):
- A sidecar-assisted e2e harness that can seed KV caches with large prefixes quickly for realistic warm-start tests. Could be infra-level job that runs nightly.
- Lightweight chaos test in canary: deliberately drop a regional pool to validate graceful fallback and that rollback works via router policy.
- Standardize PR template for runtime changes to include a (1) perf impact section, (2) observability checklist, (3) compatibility table. This PR would have benefitted from that template.

Quick TODO list (my personal ordering):
- [ ] open INF for cache size race (owner: Samir) — attach small repro and flamegraph.
- [ ] small PR for router compatibility guard (owner: Samir) — aim to land before next canary window.
- [ ] Maya to consolidate quant flags (owner: Maya) — follow-up PR post-merge.
- [ ] Jordan to add long-prefix e2e benchmark to CI (owner: Jordan) — schedule for next sprint.

Random scratch / ideas to not forget:
- Consider adding a "reason" field to the ModelVariant struct to make debugging fallbacks easier (trace it).
- For batcher: measure goroutine wake-ups per second during high throughput to ensure sleep-based backoff isn't causing spikes.
- If we consolidate caches, include an in-memory-only debug endpoint that can dump keys in sampling mode (never enabled in prod by default).

Open questions (unresolved):
- How risky is touching the batcher wake logic right before a large customer demo? Probably too risky — move to post-demo.
- Do we want to centralize metric names in a single package? Pros: consistency. Cons: churn for all PRs — need gradual migration plan.

If anything here needs to be turned into a quick issue or PR, ping me in Slack (samir) or drop a comment on PR-1428. I'll try to schedule the router guard early next week.
